translation.title: Commentary on Sūrat "al-Falaq." In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of God, glorified be His praise and hallowed be His names:
Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of al-Falaq (1) from the evil of what He created (2) and from the evil of a
when it enters (3) and from the evil of the blowers in knots (4) and from the evil of an envier when he envies (5)
He, exalted be His mention, says to His prophet Muḥammad ﷺ: say, Muḥammad: I seek protection with the Lord of al-Falaq from the evil of what He created of creation.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of al-Falaq.
Some said: it is a prison in Hell that bears this name.
Mention of those who said this:

c: al-Ḥusayn b. Yazīd al-Ṭaḥḥān told me, he said: ʿAbd al-Salām b. Ḥarb told us, from Isḥāq b. ʿAbd Allāh, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: He said: al-Falaq is a prison in Hell. [Fn 1]

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Salām b. Ḥarb told us, from Isḥāq b. ʿAbd Allāh [b. Abī Farwa, from a man] [Fn 2], from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: , he said: a prison in Hell. [Fn 2]

c: Yaʿqūb told me, he said: Hushaym told us, he said: al-ʿAwwām informed us, from [Fn 1] ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Khawlānī [Fn 2].
m: He said: A man from the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ came to Syria. He looked at the houses of the

people, at the comfort and freshness of the life they were in and at how widely they had been given room in their worldly life. He said: "I do not care [Fn 3]. Is not al-Falaq behind them?" It was said: "What is al-Falaq?" He said: "A house in Hell; when it is opened, the people of the Fire howl." [Fn 4]

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: Sufyān told us, he said: I heard al-Suddī say.
ʿAlī b. Ḥasan al-Azdī told me, he said: al-Ashjaʿī told us, from Sufyān, from al-Suddī.
Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from al-Suddī.

Isḥāq b. Wahb al-Wāsiṭī told me, he said: Masʿūd b. Mūsā b. Mushkān al-Wāsiṭī told us, he said: Naṣr b. Khuzayma al-Khurāsānī told us, from Shuʿayb b. Ṣafwān, from Muḥammad b. Kaʿb al-Qurẓī, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ.
m: He said: "al-Falaq is a covered pit (

c: Ibn al-Barqī told us, he said: Ibn Abī Maryam told us, he said: Nāfiʿ b. Yazīd told us, he said: Yaḥyā b. Abī Usayd told us, from Ibn ʿAjlān, from Abū ʿUbayd, from Kaʿb.
m: He entered a church and its beauty pleased him. He said: "The finest work, and the most misguided of people! I am content for you with al-Falaq." It was said: "What is al-Falaq?" He said: "A house in Hell; when it is opened, all the people of the Fire cry out from the intensity of its heat."

x: Others said: it is one of the names of Hell. [Fn 1]
Mention of those who said this:

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: I heard Khuthaym b. ʿAbd Allāh say: I asked Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī [Fn 2].
m: I asked about al-Falaq. He said: it is Jahannam. [Fn 1]

x: Others said: al-Falaq is the dawn (
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of al-Falaq
: he said: al-Falaq is the dawn. [Fn 3]

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī told us, he said: ʿAwf informed us, from al-Ḥasan.
m: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of al-Falaq
, he said: al-Falaq is the dawn. [Fn 1]

c: He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from Sālim al-Afṭas, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr.
m: He said: al-Falaq is the dawn. [Fn 1]

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us. And Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us. Both from Sufyān, from Sālim al-Afṭas, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr.
ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan al-Azdī told me, he said: al-Ashjaʿī told us, from Sufyān, from Sālim, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr.
Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad b. ʿAqīl, from Jābir.
m: He said: al-Falaq is the dawn.

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Abū Aḥmad told us, he said: al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ told us, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad b. ʿAqīl, from Jābir b. ʿAbd Allāh.
Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Abū Ṣakhr informed us, from al-Qurẓī.
m: He used to say about this verse
Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of al-Falaq
: he says: the splitter of the grain and the date-stone. And he recited:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us. And al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us. Both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid.
m: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of al-Falaq

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of al-Falaq
: he said: al-Falaq is the breaking of the day.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda.
m: He said: al-Falaq is the breaking of the dawn. [Fn 4]

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said.
m: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of al-Falaq
: it was said to him, "The breaking of the dawn?" He said: "Yes." And he recited:
Splitter of the daybreak, and He has made the night a time of rest

x: ), and the meaning of the verse is: say, I seek refuge in the Lord of creation.
Mention of those who said this:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās.

x: The correct view on this is to say that God, glorified be His mention, commanded His prophet Muḥammad ﷺ to say
I seek refuge in the Lord of al-Falaq
. In the speech of the Arabs,
is the breaking of the dawn; the Arabs say: "He is clearer than the
of the dawn and than the
of the dawn" [Fn 3]. It is possible that there is in Hell a prison whose name is Falaq. That being so, God did not place any indication that by
He meant one of the things called
to the exclusion of another. God, exalted be His mention, is the Lord of everything He created, so everything named
must be meant, since He is the Lord of all of it. He said
from the evil of what He created
because He commanded His prophet to seek refuge from the evil of everything, since everything besides Him is what He created.
and from the evil of a
. He says: from the evil of one that darkens when it enters and comes upon us with its darkness.
The people of interpretation then differed about the dark thing meant in this verse, from which the Messenger of God ﷺ was commanded to seek refuge.
Some of them said: it is the night when it darkens.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: and from the evil of a

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī told us, he said: ʿAwf informed us, from al-Ḥasan.
m: and from the evil of a
, he said: the beginning of the night when it darkens. [Fn 2]

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: [Abū Ṣakhr told us, from al-Qurẓī that he used to say about
h
i
ghāsiq
when it enters
. He says: the day when it enters into the night. Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said:] [Fn 3] Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from a man of the people of Medina, from Muḥammad b. Kaʿb.
m: and from the evil of a
: he said: it is the setting of the sun when night comes, when it falls due. [Fn 4]

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us. And al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us. Both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid.
m: : he said: when it comes in. [Fn 5]

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan.
m: and from the evil of a
: he said: the night when it comes on. [Fn 1]

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda, from al-Ḥasan.
m: and from the evil of a

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās.

x: Some of them said: it is the day when it enters into the night. We have mentioned this before [Fn 3].

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from a man of the people of Medina, from Muḥammad b. Kaʿb al-Qurẓī.
m: and from the evil of a
: he said: it is the setting of the sun when night comes, when it falls due. [Fn 4]

x: Others said: it is a star.
Some of them said that the star is the Pleiades (
Mention of those who said this:

c: Mujāhid b. Mūsā told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Sulaymān b. Ḥayyān informed us, from Abū al-Muhazzim, from Abū Hurayra.
m: and from the evil of a

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said.
m: , he said: The Arabs used to say: the
is the setting of the Pleiades. Diseases and plagues used to increase at its setting and cease at its rising. [Fn 1]

x: Those who say this have a ground in a report from the Prophet ﷺ, which Naṣr b. ʿAlī narrated to us.

c: Naṣr b. ʿAlī told us, he said: Bakkār b. ʿAbd Allāh, the nephew of Hammām, told us, he said: Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf told us, from his father, from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ.
m: and from the evil of a

x: when it enters is the moon. They reported a report from the Prophet ﷺ to this effect, which was narrated to us as follows.

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us. And Ibn Sufyān told us, he said: my father and Yazīd b. Hārūn told us thus. And Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Dhiʾb, from his maternal uncle al-Ḥārith b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Salama b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, [from] ʿĀʾisha.
m: She said: The Prophet ﷺ took my hand, then looked at the moon and said: "ʿĀʾisha, seek refuge in God from the evil of a
when it enters; and this is a

when it enters." This is the wording of the ḥadīth of Abū Kurayb and Ibn Wakīʿ. Ibn Ḥumayd said in his ḥadīth: She said: The Prophet ﷺ took my hand and said: "Do you know what this is? Seek refuge in God from the evil of this, for this is the

c: Muḥammad b. Sinān told us, he said: Abū ʿĀmir told us, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb told us, from al-Ḥārith b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾisha.
m: The Prophet ﷺ looked at the moon and said: "ʿĀʾisha, seek refuge in God from the evil of this, for this is the

x: The most correct of the views on this, in my opinion, is to say that God commanded His prophet ﷺ to seek refuge from the evil of a
, which is what darkens. It is said:
means: when it enters into its darkness. The night, when it enters into its darkness, is
; the star, when it sets, is
when it enters. [He did not single out] [Fn 2] any one of these but made the command general. So of every
the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to seek refuge from its evil when it enters. Qatāda used to say that the meaning of

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda.
m: : he said: when it went away. [Fn 3]

x: I do not recognize what Qatāda said here from the speech of the Arabs. What is known in their speech for the meaning of
and from the evil of the blowers in knots
. He says: from the evil of the women sorcerers who blow on knots of thread when they recite incantations over them.
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās. [Note *: Here the manuscript ṣ ends.]
m: and from the evil of the blowers in knots
: he said: whatever mixes [Fn 1] magic with incantations. [Fn 2]

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī told us, from ʿAwf, from al-Ḥasan.
m: and from the evil of the blowers in knots
: he said: the women sorcerers and the sorcerers.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, he said: Qatāda recited.
m: and from the evil of the blowers in knots
: he said: "Beware of whatever magic has mixed into these incantations." [Fn 3]

c: He said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father.
m: He said: "Nothing is nearer to polytheism than the incantation [for the snake and] [Fn 4] for the insane." [Fn 5]

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: He said: al-Ḥasan used to say, when he passed [Fn 6]
and from the evil of the blowers in knots
: "Beware of whatever magic has mixed in." [Fn 6]

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Jābir, from Mujāhid and ʿIkrima.
m: . He said: Mujāhid said: incantations on knots of thread. ʿIkrima said: the taking, in knots of thread (

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said.
m: and from the evil of the blowers in knots
: the blowers are the women sorcerers who work with the knots.

x: and from the evil of an envier when he envies
The people of interpretation differed about the envier, from whose envy the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to seek refuge.
Some said: it is every envier, and the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to seek refuge from the evil of his eye and his soul.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda.
m: and from the evil of an envier when he envies

: he said: from the evil of his eye and his soul. And from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī the same [no isnād given]. Maʿmar said: I heard Ibn Ṭāwūs narrate from his father: "The evil eye is real. If anything could outstrip the decree, the eye would outstrip it. When one of you is asked to wash (

x: Others said: rather the Prophet ﷺ was commanded in this verse to seek refuge from the evil of the Jews who envied him.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said.
m: and from the evil of an envier when he envies
, he said: the Jews [Fn 1]; nothing prevented them from believing in him except their envy. [Fn 1]

x: The more correct of the two views is the view of those who said that the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to seek refuge from the evil of every envier when he envies, whether he faults him, bewitches him or seeks harm for him. We say this because God, mighty and majestic, did not single out one envier from His saying
and from the evil of an envier when he envies
to the exclusion of another. He made His command general, to seek refuge from the evil of every envier, and so it stands on its generality.

notes.en: Al-hurar is a camel ailment involving looseness of the bowels. See Taj al-ʿArus, root h-r-r. A dog’s harir is its sound, weaker than barking, made when it can no longer bear the cold.

notes.en: Ahmad transmitted it (6/206, al-Maymaniyya edition), as did al-Baghawi in his Tafsir (8/595) and Sharh al-Sunna (5/167), through Wakiʿ. Ahmad also transmitted it (6/237) through Yazid, and al-Nasaʾi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 10138) through Sufyan. Ahmad (6/61, 215, 252, al-Maymaniyya edition), al-Tirmidhi (no. 3366), al-Hakim (2/540), and Abu al-Shaykh in al-ʿAzama (no. 681) transmitted it through Ibn Abi Dhiʾb.

notes.en: Istighsal (“requesting a wash”) means that when someone afflicted by the evil eye asks the person whose eye affected him to wash, the latter should comply. Their custom was that the afflicted person brought the person responsible a cup of water. He would put his hand in it, rinse his mouth and spit into the cup, then wash his face. He would next put in his left hand and pour water over his right, then put in his right and pour over his left; then his left hand over his right elbow, and his right over his left elbow; then his left hand over his right foot, and his right over his left foot; then his left hand over his right knee, and his right over his left knee. He would wash the inside of his lower garment. The cup was not set on the ground. The used water was then poured over the afflicted person’s head from behind, all at once, and he would recover, God willing. See al-Nihaya (3/368).
notes.ar: استغسل: أي إذا طلب من أصابته العين أن يغتسل من أصابه بعينه فليجبه، وكان من عادتهم أن الإنسان إذا أصابته عين من أحد جاء إلى العائن بقدح فيه ماء فيدخل كفه فيه، فيتمضمض ثم يمجه في القدح، ثم يغسل وجهه فيه، ثم يدخل يده اليسرى فيصب على يده اليمنى، ثم يدخل يده اليمنى فيصب على يده اليسرى، ثم يدخل يده اليسرى فيصب على مرفقه الأيمن، ثم يدخل يده اليمنى فيصب على مرفقه الأيسر، ثم يدخل يده اليسرى فيصب على قدمه اليمنى، ثم يدخل يده اليمنى فيصب على قدمه اليسرى، ثم يدخل يده اليسرى فيصب على ركبته اليمنى، ثم يدخل يده اليمنى فيصب على ركبته اليسرى، ثم يغسل داخلة إزاره، ولا يوضع القدح بالأرض، ثم يصب ذلك الماء المستعمل على رأس المصاب بالعين من خلفه صبة واحدة فيبرأ بإذن الله تعالى. النهاية 3/ 368.
